samples.summary: Materializing `lineAffinity: 'backward'` on every caret defeats the documented asymmetric selection-start default, so a shift-selection whose anchor is a wrap-boundary caret now paints from the previous visual line
samples.evidence: `moveTo` now always writes an affinity onto `position` (`lineAffinity: affinity ?? pos.lineAffinity ?? 'backward'`, cursor.ts:55; constructor line 26 too). But `cursor.position` is used verbatim as the *selection anchor* in several places — text-editor.ts:2774 (`this.selection.range?.anchor ?? pos`), :2807 (handleHome), :2826 (handleEnd), :2841 (handleDocStart), :1620 and :1572 (shift+click). `buildRects` (selection.ts:260) deliberately reads a start endpoint with **no** affinity as `'forward'` — the comment and `model/types.ts:204-208` say that default exists 'so a highlight covers the wrapped line the two endpoints bracket instead of opening on a zero-width sliver of the line above'. Before this change keyboard-derived carets carried no affinity, so anchors got that `'forward'` reading; now they carry an explicit `'backward'` (e.g. caret walked onto the boundary with ArrowLeft, which sets 'backward' at text-editor.ts:2795), and the start of the highlight resolves to the end of the previous visual line instead. The plan doc (docs/tasks/active/20260822-caret-line-affinity-todo.md:29-31) says 'absent stays reserved for endpoints from other producers … which keep computeSelectionRects' asymmetric default' — but caret-derived anchors were exactly such endpoints and no longer are, and no test covers a shift-selection anchored at a wrap boundary.

samples.summary: The comment (and the two new tests built on it) claim `recordHistoryPresence`'s narrow parameter type erased `lineAffinity` from presence at runtime; a TypeScript annotation strips nothing, so those tests pass on the pre-change code and guard nothing
samples.evidence: yorkie-doc-store.ts:2894-2897 states 'narrowing it to `{blockId, offset}` erased the wrap-boundary reading from presence after each edit — and again from what undo/redo restores'. The body is `p.set({ activeCursorPos: cursor, … })` (line 2906) — it passes the object through by reference, so any `lineAffinity` present on the object was always published; the old `pos: { blockId: string; offset: number }` annotation was type-level only. The real erasure was `Cursor.moveTo` never writing the affinity onto `position` (the item-3 problem site). Consequence: `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:408-423` and `:425-434` (which build their own `pos` with `lineAffinity: 'forward'` and pass it to `setCursorForHistory`) would also pass before this PR, so they do not pin the contract the comment says they pin, and a future re-narrowing of the caret shape *by rebuilding the object field-by-field* is what would actually break — untested.

samples.summary: Image-drop caret placement still discards the hit's affinity while the rest of the loop now propagates it, so a drop at a wrap boundary publishes the wrong reading
samples.evidence: `cursor.moveTo({ blockId: hit.blockId, offset: hit.offset })` (editor.ts:2513) drops `hit.lineAffinity`, which `paginatedPixelToPosition` returns (pagination.ts:467) and which every other mouse-derived path carries (text-editor.ts:1521-1525, :1622-1625). With the new invariant that the caret always states its reading, this site now silently states `'backward'` for a drop that landed on the start of a continuation visual line, and that value is what presence/history publish. Low severity: the pre-change behaviour was identical, but the diff's stated goal ('a future call site that forgets it gets the position's own reading') is not achieved here because the affinity is stripped before `moveTo` ever sees it.
